name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Luke Bronin's large fundraising and outside support advantage
Open seat after Larson lost renomination
model.rationale: The seat sits in D+12 territory and Democrats hold every structural advantage: Bronin has raised over $3 million with substantial outside backing, while Republican Amy Chai has raised about $21,000 with almost no cash on hand. Markets price a Democratic win near 95%, and the only real uncertainty is the open-seat transition.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though a flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's first district is an open seat after longtime incumbent John Larson lost renomination, with former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin carrying the Democratic banner against Republican Amy Chai. The district leans heavily Democratic, and Bronin has built a commanding financial position, raising over $3 million and benefiting from more than $1.3 million in outside support. Chai has raised roughly $21,000 and reports only a few hundred dollars on hand, leaving her with minimal resources for a competitive campaign.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 95%, and no independent polls or expert ratings are available to challenge that picture. The open-seat transition adds some uncertainty, but the combination of district lean and the fundraising gap makes a Democratic hold the clear expectation, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
